⌋
[SWS_CM_00138] Minimum Send Interval monitoring for transmission requests
for events
⌈
To protect receivers from flooding/overload, each event shall have a config-
urable Minimum Send Interval (see
ServiceInterfaceDeploymentElement
.
min-
imumSendInterval
), which specifies the minimum amount of time that shall pass
between two consecutive transmissions, i.e., the Minimum Send Interval limits the
maximum Tx frequency of a given event in the network. If the application requests
transmission of an event by calling
Event::Send()/Send()
,
ara::com
shall check,
whether the time since the last successful handover of the Event to the underlying
transmission layer is greater than the specified Minimum Send Interval, i.e., the Mini-
mum Send Interval is not violated. If the event has never been sent before, this shall
also successfully pass the Minimum Send Interval check. If the Minimum Send In-
terval is not violated,
ara::com
shall process the transmission request by handing
over the event to the transmission layer. The time of handover shall count as start
of the new Minimum Send Interval monitoring. If the Minimum Send Interval is vio-
lated,
ara::com
shall discard the transmission request and return error
ComErrc::
kMinimumSendIntervalViolationError
(see [SWS_CM_10432]). If the config-
ured Minimum Send Interval (
ServiceInterfaceDeploymentElement
.
minimum-
SendInterval
) of an event has the value 0, the Minimum Send Interval monitoring
shall not be active for the corresponding event.
